title: SLO-aligned alert triage ranking and regional throttle playbook
creator: Amina Patel
description: Objective: Reduce on-call noise while preserving fast detection of user-impacting SLO violations across multi-region deployments. Deliver an SLO-driven alert scoring model, a staged regional throttle (soft-throttle) mechanism that ties into existing circuit breakers, and a single canonical runbook that can be invoked automatically or manually to perform graceful load shedding and failover.
design_decisions: Alert scoring is computed by combining SLO breach probability, user impact weight, and signal freshness into a single 0-100 score.
Threshold buckets: <30 = informative (no page), 30-60 = notify (Slack), 60-80 = on-call page (primary), 80+ = urgent page + regional failover candidate.
Soft-throttle: a regional request admission control that reduces new request acceptance by percentiles rather than hard reject; integrates with circuit-breaker state to escalate.
Graceful shedding order: background batch work -> low-priority realtime routes -> high-importance routes last, based on route metadata.
Automation: Score crossing 60 triggers automated enrichment + runbook suggestion; score crossing 80 will trigger a dry-run failover in the canary region before executing global failover.
We intentionally decouple scoring from Prometheus alert firing rules. Prometheus rules annotate signals and push events into the scoring service for final decisioning.
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: On page, consult the SLO alert scoring panel (Dashboard: SLO-Alert-Scoring). Verify score, affected region(s), and top failing routes.
2) Enrichment: Click 'Enrich' to fetch recent traces, recent KV cache miss histogram, kernel latency percentiles, and GPU utilization snapshots.
3) Soft-throttle: If score >= 60 and regional p95 latency > SLO by 25% for 2m, enable regional soft-throttle at 20% and monitor 1m; document command in notes.
4) Circuit breaker: If soft-throttle fails to reduce score after 3 minutes or score >= 80, escalate to open region circuit-breaker at 75% error budget consumption for the region.

5) Failover plan: When circuit-breaker opens, perform staged failover: (a) shift 10% cross-region traffic to healthy region, (b) increase to 50% if metrics improve in 2m, (c) if stable, cutover remaining traffic.
6) Rollback: If downstream errors increase or SLO regressions worsen, roll back the staged failover and close the circuit-breaker; file a postmortem if customer impact > 10% requests.
7) Post-incident: Run the incident checklist: label root cause, attach dashboards/PRs, update SLO alert scoring weights if false positives were identified, and schedule follow-up engineering work.

8) Automation hooks: Use /runbook trigger to kick off the automation play that (a) creates an incident channel, (b) posts the top enrichment artifacts, and (c) queues a canary failover job in the orchestration service.
metrics_and_dashboards: p95 latency by route and region
KV cache hit ratio and growth in cache miss prefix
Model-inference GPU utilization, kernel stall counts
Circuit-breaker state timeline and open duration
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for scoring function (edge cases: stale signals, missing tags).
2) Integration test that simulates cascading latency in us-west and verifies soft-throttle enacted at expected score thresholds.
3) Game-day: Controlled canary where we inject 40% additional synthetic latency into eu-central for 10 minutes to validate staged failover and rollback behavior.
4) Chaos test: Randomly flip regional circuit-breakers in a staging cluster to ensure runbook automation recovers gracefully.
implementation_notes: Backend: scoring-service will run as a small stateful deployment that consumes alerts and traces; enrichments fetched via async workers.
API: add /score endpoint returning score and 'suggested_action' for automation to consume.
Orchestration: reuse existing failover orchestration with a new 'soft-throttle' action and 'staged-failover' workflow.
Observability: add tagging to traces when soft-throttle or staged-failover is active to enable post-incident attribution.
